key_insight: Plasma proteomics divided ALS patients into three molecular subgroups with distinct survival outcomes, revealing biologically different disease patterns.
clinical_relevance: This approach could support more precise ALS patient stratification beyond standard clinical features and may help identify groups with different prognoses.
method: Profiled ~5,400 plasma proteins in 235 ALS patients using Olink Explore HT
Applied consensus clustering to identify patient subgroups
Used WGCNA, GO analysis, and cell-type enrichment to interpret protein modules and origins
evidence_signal: The abstract reports three clusters with significantly different survival outcomes, with the shorter-survival group showing stress-response and Rho-GTPase-related protein modules.
watch_item: Findings come from a single study cohort, so external validation and reproducibility in independent ALS populations are still needed.
paper_title: Molecular subgroups of ALS patients with distinct survival outcomes identified through plasma proteomics
